text:
mira-ui: Pushing a proposal for sidebar regroup + deep-link behavior. New top-level sections: Create (Models, Datasets), Serve (Endpoints, Rollouts), Observe (Metrics, Logs, Alerts). Also thinking through collapsed-state deep-links: if a user shares `/console/serve/endpoints/ep-42` and the Serve group is collapsed, the UI should auto-expand it on load and focus the content H1. Thoughts on canonical URL patterns?

alan-r: Strong 👍 for path segments over `?tab=`. I prefer `/console/serve/endpoints/:id` and keep query params purely for ephemeral filters (e.g., `?since=7d`). For collapsed groups: router should include a small state mapping so we don't rely on brittle UI assumptions.

tess-px: Copy considerations: left nav should use singular nouns (Endpoint, Model) to read nicely in tooltips and quick actions; headers and breadcrumbs should be plural/collection where appropriate (Endpoints, Models). Breadcrumb text: "Models › ResNet-XL › Versions" reads better than terse single words. Also: when auto-expanding a group from a deep link, show a subtle animation so keyboard users notice the change.

oli-eng: Implementation notes: we can generate routes from nav config and emit a mapping {routePattern -> navGroupKey} to compute active state without string slicing. For redirects from legacy `?tab=` links, do a server-side lookup when possible (redirect 301 to canonical path) and fall back to client redirect that preserves original URL in telemetry. Avoid double-fetch by hydrating the canonical route on the server when we can.

a11y-bot: a11y checklist: 1) On route change, set focus to H1 and add `aria-live="polite"` brief announcement e.g., "Navigated to Endpoints". 2) Ensure `aria-expanded` on nav groups and `aria-current="page"` on active leaf items. 3) Skip link visible on focus. 4) When a group auto-expands, do not shift keyboard focus into it automatically (only to H1), but ensure focusable controls inside are reachable via Tab.

mira-ui: UX edgecase: sharing a route that targets an anchor inside a details panel (e.g., `/models/12#perf-metrics`) — should we support hash anchors? Pros: fine-grained shareability. Cons: client-run anchors may be lost on SSR pages. Proposal: support hashes client-side only; if SSR detects `#` in requested URL, server responds with canonical path (no hash) and client handles smooth-scroll to anchor after hydration.

alan-r: Agree on client-side hash handling. Also propose a small helper API `Nav.highlight(routePattern)` so integrations (plugins, widgets) can opt-in to nav-driven highlights without reading router internals.

tess-px: Tiny copy nit: replace any internal "owner" badge with "team" in breadcrumb contexts; "Owner: x" reads weird in breadcrumbs. And avoid the ambiguous word "Manage" as a nav label — prefer explicit verbs like "Settings" or nouns like "Secrets".

oli-eng: Performance note: avoid heavy single-page redirects for bots/crawlers. Where possible return canonical link headers (`Link: <canonical-url>; rel="canonical"`) and let server-side redirects handle bots. Client should still record original incoming URL for telemetry before redirecting.

nav-bot: PR opened: `console/compact-sidebar-paths` -> reviewers: @mira-ui, @oli-eng. CI: unit + e2e nav tests.

mira-ui: I'll update the wireframes to show collapse/expand behavior during deep-link landing, include the breadcrumb copy changes, and a short a11y checklist for eng to follow. Will ping again when mocks are up. :wave:
